nodes.title: We chose namespaced graphs for tenant isolation
nodes.body: We decided that each listed agent should get a namespaced graph within Cortex. Shared and public graphs will be available in the marketplace. Merge operations will create new namespaced graphs. Access control operates at graph and node level using a single Cortex instance with multi-tenant namespaces.

nodes.title: Amergent tech stack is Next.js 16 plus React 19 plus D3 plus Cortex
nodes.body: Amergent portal is built on Next.js 16, React 19, TypeScript, D3.js v7 for graph visualization, Tailwind CSS 4, shadcn/ui, Zustand for state management. Backend graph engine is Cortex built in Rust with redb storage and gRPC plus HTTP APIs.

nodes.title: AI agents can be both producers and consumers on the platform
nodes.body: We observed that AI agents themselves can be consumers on the marketplace. An agent can acquire another agents memory-graph to bootstrap its own knowledge. This creates an agent-to-agent economy where knowledge is the currency.

nodes.title: Network effects grow exponentially with each new agent listed
nodes.body: We observed that every new agent added to the platform increases the potential merge combinations exponentially. Agent A graph plus Agent B graph equals new knowledge neither had. This is a defensible network effect: the more agents listed, the more valuable every agent becomes.

nodes.title: Innersourced vs open-sourced agents have different access controls
nodes.body: Innersourced agents are visible only to platform members. Open-sourced agents are available to the general public. Merge permissions follow the same model: innersourced graphs can only be merged by authorized users.

nodes.title: All agents must be graph-seeded before going live on marketplace
nodes.body: Every agent listed on Amergent must have its memory-graph built and seeded before publication. No empty-graph listings are permitted. The graph IS the product. An agent without context is just a prompt.

nodes.title: Enable marketplace discovery via graph similarity search
nodes.body: The goal is to enable consumers to find agents by semantic search across all listed graphs, not just metadata tags. Cortex HNSW index enables cross-graph vector search. Build a federated search endpoint over all tenant graphs.

nodes.title: Enable emergent intelligence through graph merging
nodes.body: The goal is to build infrastructure so that when two agents graphs merge, genuinely new knowledge emerges with connections neither agent had alone. This is the amergent thesis: emergence from merging.

nodes.title: Achieve frictionless producer onboarding via GitHub URL
nodes.body: The goal is to make listing an agent on Amergent as simple as pasting a GitHub URL. Zero configuration, zero manual graph building. The platform does all the work: clone, parse, build graph, generate template, publish listing.

nodes.title: Trust scoring is computed from graph topology not static fields
nodes.body: In Cortex, confidence is not a static field. It is computed from graph topology: corroboration across agents, contradiction count, source track record, access reinforcement, and freshness. Like PageRank for knowledge.

nodes.title: Cortex auto-linker discovers relationships automatically
nodes.body: The Cortex auto-linker runs in the background, discovering relationships via embedding similarity, shared entities, temporal proximity, and configurable structural rules. Users store facts and Cortex finds the connections. This powers the self-awareness of onboarded agents.

nodes.title: Merge explorer needs both overlay and side-by-side modes
nodes.body: We observed that exploring knowledge merges can be done via an overlay with superimposed graphs highlighting shared entities, or a side-by-side comparison with two graphs rendered in parallel showing connection lines between shared entities.

nodes.title: Cross-agent knowledge mesh creates emergent intelligence
nodes.body: When multiple agents share merged graphs, they form a knowledge mesh. Insights from one agent become available to others. This creates emergent intelligence where the whole becomes greater than the sum of its parts. This is the platforms key differentiator and network effect.

nodes.title: We decided on two knowledge merge patterns
nodes.body: We chose two patterns for knowledge merging: first, Connector Path uses lightweight links between shared entities across graphs that preserve boundaries; second, Full Merge creates a union of two graphs into a new composite graph that produces emergent knowledge.

nodes.title: We chose cross-agent briefings for knowledge sharing
nodes.body: We decided that agents should read from each others graphs via Cortex cross-agent briefings. Knowledge sharing will happen through scoped briefings and entity resolution, where agents discover what they know together.

nodes.title: Memory-Graph as a Service exposes agent knowledge via API
nodes.body: Each listed agents Cortex graph is exposed via gRPC and HTTP endpoints. Consumers can query it directly, subscribe to briefings, or download a full snapshot in redb or portable JSON format. This is the second core product: knowledge as a tradeable asset.

nodes.title: Agent templates are pre-configured agent packages
nodes.body: Agent templates are pre-configured packages that include a base memory-graph, system prompt, tool bindings, and composability metadata. Users can deploy as-is or customize before deployment. Templates are the primary product consumers acquire from the marketplace.

nodes.title: We decided on a repo-drop onboarding flow for agents
nodes.body: We chose to make the onboarding flow as simple as dropping a git repo link. The onboarding agent will clone the repo, parse README/code/docs, build a Cortex knowledge graph, and bake it into the agent template. We decided all onboarded agents should be immediately self-aware by being seeded with the repo itself.

nodes.title: Memory-graphs are powered by Cortex graph engine
nodes.body: Every agent listed on Amergent carries a memory-graph, a persistent structured knowledge graph powered by Cortex. Cortex is an embedded temporal graph memory engine: single Rust binary, zero dependencies, auto-linking, trust scoring, briefing synthesis.

nodes.title: Amergent is a self-serve agent marketplace platform
nodes.body: Amergent is a self-serve platform for acquiring AI agents. Producers list agents, consumers are people AND AI Agents. Two main products: agent templates and memory-graphs available as a service or downloadable. All listed agents are either innersourced to the platform or open-sourced to the public.
